title: Creating Nails in CLO3D – No Extra Software Needed
content:
![bbf80d9a2a814a3f8a4de67e6a77fb9b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/c9633dd4f90a460e94ace3a5f339702e/images/bbf80d9a2a814a3f8a4de67e6a77fb9bUntitled%20design-7.png)

Whenever I post an outfit or create final renders for personal projects or clients, I like to go the extra mile - not only finishing the clothes down to the last detail, but also adding accessories like **nails** 💅.

The odd thing? There are only a few nail assets in the CLO library.

The good thing? It’s surprisingly easy to make your own! ✨

* * *

# **For a simple manicure:**

  1. Download the **arm folding image** file

  2. Paint the nails in your chosen color

  3. Export as **PNG**

  4. Replace the original arm folding image with your new one




# **For a more detailed nail set:**

  1. Create the nail base using a small curved pattern (like you’d make a rigid trim)

  2. Shape and scale it to match the avatar’s nail bed

  3. Use **pins** and **internal lines** to position and curve it around the finger

  4. Apply **thickness** and **texture** to simulate polish, gloss, or nail art

  5. Freeze to avoid deformation during simulation




* * *

By creating nails this way, you can manually place and pose them on the avatar.

But keep in mind: **adding the nails should be the very last step before rendering** , since fabric-based nails do **not follow** avatar poses.

# **Why not convert them into accessories?**

I’ve tried that - but here’s the limitation:

CLO accessories can’t be rigged to individual fingers. So the nails stay locked in place, not following hand or finger movement. That’s why I recommend leaving them as fabric-based nails. It’s the most flexible solution!

Have you tried making nails yourself? Or found another hack to do it faster? 👀

By the way - this is a render of my most recent nail asset! It’s now available for purchase on my profile. Go check it out! 💥

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Great tip! Thank you. I will try to do my own nails 💅
Reply 1: Do it! Add some internal lines in the middle to make them slightly curved😉
content_description: This page guides CLO users on how to create custom fabric-based nail assets for detailed outfit renders, offering step-by-step tips and explaining why this method is more flexible than using accessories.

title: Why is my render in low quality even though Im using a good PC, NVIDIA graphics and nice set-ups?
content:
I spent 30 min rendering this image but as you can see it below, it turn out like crap. What am I doing wrong? Im so tired, what dont know what else to do. Do I need to wait for the render preview to load completely? And if I do, why does it keep stuck for half a hour in the same spot?

![8ab6a332721c452ea461818e137d69a9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/8ab6a332721c452ea461818e137d69a9Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152210.png)![5adf0e95a6ef4517a111076334cac5f5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/5adf0e95a6ef4517a111076334cac5f5render2.jpg)![61a29081c912486b86ab87cdd8cd7b79](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/61a29081c912486b86ab87cdd8cd7b79Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152255.png)![223b5a91fabc4a0b9660ded38f899404](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/223b5a91fabc4a0b9660ded38f899404Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152409.png)![31e6466adad04064badcc025cacd77cd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/31e6466adad04064badcc025cacd77cdScreenshot%202025-07-07%20152237.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Looks amazing and like you have it all sorted out...I just thought even the first image looked high quality, just blurred. My thought was to uncheck Depth of Field.

Comment 2: A few other pointersNoise : 0.030 is the lowest we recommend. The human eye will not see the difference and reducing to 0.010 will just increase the time it takesQuality for both Material & Light. This is about how light bounces in a scene. Unless you are building scenes with walls/furniture where light has places to bounce. Keeping it at Medium is usually ok. Since the dress it metallic I would maybe increase material to High

Comment 3: Did you click the second button or the first? In the photo I circled the right button to left click. The first one does not do the render. When the render is done a popup window will appear and will lead you to the folder where your render image was saved.

Comment 4: Hi, did you use "focus by left click" by any chance under Depth of Field? Could you tick off Physical Camera completely and try again? (On a general note, please see this article: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f
Reply 1: hi! it does look better, but that is so weird.... my teacher in CLO3D at uni told me to put exact this values and in his file it worked...
Reply 2: this was our first try together, with exact the same parameters and it worked!
Reply 3: Hi Barbara, the focus by left click can produce blurry results based on where you left-click on the image. I like to use it to get a more "photographed"-looking output, but you just have to play with it a bit and see what result you like. It is best to use it and click after you've already decided on the angle and cutout you want. It will be taken into account by the interactive render, so you can have it load a bit and see if you really want to render this output before you do. Hope this helps!
content_description: A place to seek advice and troubleshoot issues related to slow or poor-quality image rendering and stuck render previews.

Comment 7: If the garment was not arranged properly then yes you would need to arrange again if the garment fell off. You will also want to check and make sure that all of your sewing is correct as well. If the sewing is criss cross or incorrect that can cause collision and the garment can also fall offPlease add images of the garment arranged, but before simulationWe would also recommend keeping the avatar at the center of the scene and standing straight while building. Putting the avatar at a non optimal position like this will not be good for buildingTip : Take your time and double check everything. Pattern pieces are all placed on the avatar near where they will end up and not inside the avatar. Sewing is nice and straight, no twisting or passing through the inside of the avatar.

title: exploding animation issue

Since update 2025.0, animation mode has changed and it happens that the exploding garment animation no longer works the way explained in this tutorial :[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CrCs-yNL5EY&t=372s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CrCs-yNL5EY&t=372s)

Comment 1: Hi, the recording button is not used in the tutorial and it still works the same way. The reason the recording button is not necessary is because there are no actual pattern pieces in the scene that have to be simulated to movement, only OBJs morphing into each other.
